# Machine SM factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agentic-workflows:
# the frozen machine-loop home. GitHub requires reusable workflows at the
# .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# Migrated from IstiN/dmtools-agents factory-sm.yml (f377609) — the
# agents-repo copy is DEPRECATED for new callers (kept only so existing
# pinned users like fa keep resolving their historical SHA).
#
# FREEZE CONTRACT: target repositories carry only a thin stub (schedule +
# this call) pinned to an immutable SHA of THIS repo. Agent code and the
# dmtools CLI are NOT tied to that SHA anymore — they resolve from RELEASES
# by version knobs (repo variables of the CALLER, per-repo, no workflow
# edits to bump):
#
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION   — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' or e.g.
#                           'agents-rel-20260928-…'); the agent pack
#                           (sm_github) is fetched from that release's
#                           asset catalog via the dmtools registry
#                           (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY). Default: latest.
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION  — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' or
#                           'vX.Y.Z'); installed from the release bundle.
#                           Default: latest.
#
# Runs in the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo,
# vars.* and secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own
# versions).
#
# What it does: resolves the two version knobs, installs the dmtools CLI
# (release asset, no repo file needed), then runs the SM rule engine as a
# VERSIONED AGENT PACK (dmtools run sm_github@latest) against the target
# repo's loop state — the pack carries smAgent.js + rules + engine closure,
# verified against the release's sha256 inventory.
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     schedule: [{cron: '*/10 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {dryRun: {type: boolean, default: true}}}
#   jobs:
#     sm:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}   # STRING —
#         # typed (boolean) reusable inputs reject expressions; strings take them.
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine SM'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      dryRun:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions, live bisect probes D/E)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login for #687 PR rules: excluded from review-external-once, gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews and the SM prMachineAuthor rules (auto legs, e.g. auto rework). Global-level knob — the agents repo carries no hardcoded login."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      silent-token:
        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows. Routed as an INPUT: GitHub delivers an EMPTY value when github.token is mapped through the reusable-call secrets block (live-verified), while inputs carry it; GitHub auto-masks token values in logs either way."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      ci-workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'quality.yml'
      validation-checks:
        description: "Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps these check names itself. JSON array as a STRING (e.g. '[\"agents-suite\",\"static\",\"gate\"]')."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      parallel-workers:
        description: "OPT-IN (dmtools Dart runtime only): runAsync worker-pool size for parallel READ fan-out inside the SM tick (per-PR/issue enrichment, dispatched-CI probes). '0'/absent = runAsync not wired — the engine takes its sequential fallback (Java/GraalJS parity), zero deviation. A value parsing to int >= 2 rides jobParams.parallelWorkers."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '0'
      state-publish:
        description: "OPT-IN factory-state publishing (owner 2026-09-23): JSON object {channel:'release', repo?, tag?, asset?}. The tick uploads factory-state.json as a public prerelease asset; the board (site/factory) reads the releases/latest CDN link. Empty = off."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the callee
# does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing declared one fails
# the guard test (factory_stub_ref_test.dart parity in each caller).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: "PAT for GitHub tool calls + gh CLI (SM engine + validation probes)."
        required: true
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN:
        description: "Optional dedicated silent-update token; the silent-token input wins when both are set."
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

env:
  # Version knobs resolve from the CALLER's repository variables (vars.*
  # resolve in the caller's context for reusable workflows) — bumping an
  # agent/CLI version is a repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
  AGENTS_VERSION: ${{ vars.AGENTS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'latest' }}

jobs:
  sm:
    name: sm / reconcile
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The pack runner resolves .dmtools/config.js from the CWD —
          # the target repo root (machineAuthor, jira.fields, ...).
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve versions (agents release + dmtools CLI)
        # 'latest' resolves to the newest PUBLISHED release tag at tick
        # time; an explicit tag (e.g. vars.AGENTS_VERSION=agents-rel-…)
        # pins the tick reproducibly. Fails loudly when the tag does not
        # exist (gh api exits non-zero → red tick, no silent fallback).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          resolve_tag() {
            local repo="$1" knob="$2"
            if [ "$knob" = "latest" ]; then
              gh api "repos/${repo}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name
            else
              # existence check — a typo'd pin must fail HERE, not in the tick
              gh api "repos/${repo}/releases/tags/${knob}" --jq .tag_name
            fi
          }
          AGENTS_TAG="$(resolve_tag IstiN/dmtools-agents "$AGENTS_VERSION")"
          DMTOOLS_TAG="$(resolve_tag epam/dmtools-dart "$DMTOOLS_VERSION")"
          echo "AGENTS_TAG=${AGENTS_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "DMTOOLS_TAG=${DMTOOLS_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "agents pack release: ${AGENTS_TAG} (knob: ${AGENTS_VERSION})"
          echo "dmtools CLI release: ${DMTOOLS_TAG} (knob: ${DMTOOLS_VERSION})"

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (release bundle)
        # The installer ships as a release asset, version-locked to the
        # bundle it installs — no copy of install.sh in the target repo.
        run: |

          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_TAG}"

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

blocks.text:
# Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding)

The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your
`recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and
drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI
minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction
(severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged.

## Verdict mapping

Classify findings exactly as instructed:

- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing
  gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR
  works as shipped.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish.

Then map to the verdict:

| Findings | `recommendation` |
|---|---|
| Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss |
| No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` |

`APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state
(`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as
before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge
and must **not** trigger another rework round.

## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71)

- ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new
  suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle
  with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`.
- ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine
  treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep
  `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose.
  The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments
  (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment
  file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly
  blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+.
- ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text.
  The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict.
- ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff —
  add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead.

## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30)

`chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs
may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a
factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride
the lane independently). Reviews must therefore:

- ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup,
  not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it
  from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue
  for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed).
- ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via
  another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other
  PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours.
- ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review
  comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine
  only merges.

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      ((github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a queued twin run
    # behind the per-issue concurrency group (live dmd gh-317/gh-318); the
    # in-run dedupe cannot act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole
    # run pending before any job starts. Leg dispatching is dispatch-only
    # (SM workflow_dispatch; manual rework override #544 = dispatch leg=rework).
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, minimal read: job-level grants below carry
# the real rights (SEC-08 review #849, thread -1oD — a top-level write block
# becomes the default for every future job in this workflow). The factory
# job's own permissions block mirrors the pinned callee's declared scopes
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
# #796).
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Read-only: this job only resolves assignees/inputs and echoes outputs.
    # It inherits the workflow-level read-only default and must NOT see the
    # factory job's write scopes (SEC-08 review, #796).
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

  factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.g…

blocks.text:
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@f59104948fec3e8dc5fe5b26fa92e538f73a5019
    with:
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @f59104948fec3e8dc5fe5b26fa92e538f73a5019 — ships:
    # #579 (conflict-rework: PR-anchored dispatch when no OPEN linked
    # issue — DIRTY machines PRs no longer dead-letter on closed issues),
    # #577/#578 (mutexExcludeSelf by fact of holding: a self-holding
    # candidate IS the holder — two approved ai_validating arms no longer
    # block each other into a total queue freeze; live fa #1068+#1088
    # 2026-09-30, ~40 min deadlock), #576 (review-machine-unlinked: a
    # MACHINE-authored validated PR with no OPEN linked issue gets its
    # one-time review — fixes the validated-forever starvation, live fa
    # #1068 19h / #1071 / #1075), #573 (every pack release is a
    # self-contained snapshot), #574 (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY passed into
    # the agent run env), #572 (review-stale-verdict-unchecked: a
    # validated+reviewed PR whose head lost its checks gets a re-REVIEW
    # first; final validation stays in validate-armed), #571 (factory
    # teammate leg self-heals a broken dmtools install), #570 (SM
    # workflow budget 1 -> 3), #569 (rework: a fatal CLI failure is no
    # longer announced as "Rework Complete"),
    # #568 (mergeBot workspace/repository args), #566 (pack-registry
    # runner overrides).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@f59104948fec3e8dc5fe5b26fa92e538f73a5019
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Machine SM factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agentic-workflows:
# the frozen machine-loop home. GitHub requires reusable workflows at the
# .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# Migrated from IstiN/dmtools-agents factory-sm.yml (f377609) — the
# agents-repo copy is DEPRECATED for new callers (kept only so existing
# pinned users like fa keep resolving their historical SHA).
#
# FREEZE CONTRACT: target repositories carry only a thin stub (schedule +
# this call) pinned to an immutable SHA of THIS repo. Agent code and the
# dmtools CLI are NOT tied to that SHA anymore — they resolve from RELEASES
# by version knobs (repo variables of the CALLER, per-repo, no workflow
# edits to bump):
#
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION   — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' or e.g.
#                           'agents-rel-20260928-…'); the agent pack
#                           (sm_github) is fetched from that release's
#                           asset catalog via the dmtools registry
#                           (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY). Default: latest.
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION  — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' or
#                           'vX.Y.Z'); installed from the release bundle.
#                           Default: latest.
#
# Runs in the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo,
# vars.* and secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own
# versions).
#
# What it does: resolves the two version knobs, installs the dmtools CLI
# (release asset, no repo file needed), then runs the SM rule engine as a
# VERSIONED AGENT PACK (dmtools run sm_github@latest) against the target
# repo's loop state — the pack carries smAgent.js + rules + engine closure,
# verified against the release's sha256 inventory.
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     schedule: [{cron: '*/10 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {dryRun: {type: boolean, default: true}}}
#   jobs:
#     sm:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}   # STRING —
#         # typed (boolean) reusable inputs reject expressions; strings take them.
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine SM'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      dryRun:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions, live bisect probes D/E)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login for #687 PR rules: excluded from review-external-once, gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews and the SM prMachineAuthor rules (auto legs, e.g. auto rework). Global-level knob — the agents repo carries no hardcoded login."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      silent-token:
        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows. Routed as an INPUT: GitHub delivers an EMPTY value when github.token is mapped through the reusable-call secrets block (live-verified), while inputs carry it; GitHub auto-masks token values in logs either way."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      ci-workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'quality.yml'
      validation-checks:
        description: "Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps these check names itself. JSON array as a STRING (e.g. '[\"agents-suite\",\"static\",\"gate\"]')."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      parallel-workers:
        description: "OPT-IN (dmtools Dart runtime only): runAsync worker-pool size for parallel READ fan-out inside the SM tick (per-PR/issue enrichment, dispatched-CI probes). '0'/absent = runAsync not wired — the engine takes its sequential fallback (Java/GraalJS parity), zero deviation. A value parsing to int >= 2 rides jobParams.parallelWorkers."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '0'
      state-publish:
        description: "OPT-IN factory-state publishing (owner 2026-09-23): JSON object {channel:'release', repo?, tag?, asset?}. The tick uploads factory-state.json as a public prerelease asset; the board (site/factory) reads the releases/latest CDN link. Empty = off."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the callee
# does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing declared one fails
# the guard test (factory_stub_ref_test.dart parity in each caller).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: "PAT for GitHub tool calls + gh CLI (SM engine + validation probes)."
        required: true
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN:
        description: "Optional dedicated silent-update token; the silent-token input wins when both are set."
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

env:
  # Version knobs resolve from the CALLER's repository variables (vars.*
  # resolve in the caller's context for reusable workflows) — bumping an
  # agent/CLI version is a repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
  AGENTS_VERSION: ${{ vars.AGENTS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'latest' }}

jobs:
  sm:
    name: sm / reconcile
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The pack runner resolves .dmtools/config.js from the CWD —
          # the target repo root (machineAuthor, jira.fields, ...).
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve versions (agents release + dmtools CLI)
        # 'latest' resolves to the newest PUBLISHED release tag at tick
        # time; an explicit tag (e.g. vars.AGENTS_VERSION=agents-rel-…)
        # pins the tick reproducibly. Fails loudly when the tag does not
        # exist (gh api exits non-zero → red tick, no silent fallback).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          resolve_tag() {
            local repo="$1" knob="$2"
            if [ "$knob" = "latest" ]; then
              gh api "repos/${repo}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name
            else
              # existence check — a typo'd pin must fail HERE, not in the tick
              gh api "repos/${repo}/releases/tags/${knob}" --jq .tag_name
            fi
          }
          AGENTS_TAG="$(resolve_tag IstiN/dmtools-agents "$AGENTS_VERSION")"
          DMTOOLS_TAG="$(resolve_tag epam/dmtools-dart "$DMTOOLS_VERSION")"
          echo "AGENTS_TAG=${AGENTS_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "DMTOOLS_TAG=${DMTOOLS_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "agents pack release: ${AGENTS_TAG} (knob: ${AGENTS_VERSION})"
          echo "dmtools CLI release: ${DMTOOLS_TAG} (knob: ${DMTOOLS_VERSION})"

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (release bundle)
        # The installer ships as a release asset, version-locked to the
        # bundle it installs — no copy of install.sh in the target repo.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_TAG}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_TAG}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

blocks.text:
# Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding)

The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your
`recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and
drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI
minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction
(severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged.

## Verdict mapping

Classify findings exactly as instructed:

- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing
  gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR
  works as shipped.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish.

Then map to the verdict:

| Findings | `recommendation` |
|---|---|
| Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss |
| No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` |

`APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state
(`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as
before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge
and must **not** trigger another rework round.

## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71)

- ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new
  suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle
  with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`.
- ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine
  treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep
  `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose.
  The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments
  (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment
  file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly
  blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+.
- ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text.
  The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict.
- ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff —
  add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead.

## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30)

`chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs
may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a
factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride
the lane independently). Reviews must therefore:

- ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup,
  not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it
  from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue
  for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed).
- ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via
  another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other
  PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours.
- ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review
  comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine
  only merges.

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      ((github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a queued twin run
    # behind the per-issue concurrency group (live dmd gh-317/gh-318); the
    # in-run dedupe cannot act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole
    # run pending before any job starts. Leg dispatching is dispatch-only
    # (SM workflow_dispatch; manual rework override #544 = dispatch leg=rework).
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, minimal read: job-level grants below carry
# the real rights (SEC-08 review #849, thread -1oD — a top-level write block
# becomes the default for every future job in this workflow). The factory
# job's own permissions block mirrors the pinned callee's declared scopes
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
# #796).
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:

      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||

                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@f59104948fec3e8dc5fe5b26fa92e538f73a5019
    with:
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @f59104948fec3e8dc5fe5b26fa92e538f73a5019 — ships:
    # #579 (conflict-rework: PR-anchored dispatch when no OPEN linked
    # issue — DIRTY machines PRs no longer dead-letter on closed issues),
    # #577/#578 (mutexExcludeSelf by fact of holding: a self-holding
    # candidate IS the holder — two approved ai_validating arms no longer
    # block each other into a total queue freeze; live fa #1068+#1088
    # 2026-09-30, ~40 min deadlock), #576 (review-machine-unlinked: a
    # MACHINE-authored validated PR with no OPEN linked issue gets its
    # one-time review — fixes the validated-forever starvation, live fa
    # #1068 19h / #1071 / #1075), #573 (every pack release is a
    # self-contained snapshot), #574 (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY passed into
    # the agent run env), #572 (review-stale-verdict-unchecked: a
    # validated+reviewed PR whose head lost its checks gets a re-REVIEW
    # first; final validation stays in validate-armed), #571 (factory
    # teammate leg self-heals a broken dmtools install), #570 (SM
    # workflow budget 1 -> 3), #569 (rework: a fatal CLI failure is no
    # longer announced as "Rework Complete"),
    # #568 (mergeBot workspace/repository args), #566 (pack-registry
    # runner overrides).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@f59104948fec3e8dc5fe5b26fa92e538f73a5019
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

          # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,

          # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
          # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
          # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
          # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
          # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
          # a fallback when the API read itself fails.

            # status transition echoes back as a `labeled` event and would
            # re-derive the same leg on top of itself.
            # #544: manual agent:rework is the owner override — it fires
            # rework even from a `labeled` event, but only when the labeler
            # has write/admin (see rework_override_ok). Without permission
            # the override is ignored (runner stays empty → clean skip).
            if rework_override_ok; then

            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then

            # sets it as the "ready for review" invitation, so blocking on it
            # kills the label-echo review trigger (live: dmtools-dart gh-182).
            # Real duplicate protection is the per-issue concurrency group.
            runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW"; slot="review"
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qE 'status:In Development|status:In Review|status:In Rework|in progress|ai_developed|ai_pr_reviewed|_wip|rework-round-'; then
            # Dev is a FRESH handoff only: once the loop has touched the
            # issue, later `labeled` events (the dev leg's OWN status:In
            # Development transition, SM backfill labels, ...) would
            # re-derive dev and queue a duplicate leg on top of the
            # running/finished one (live: fa gh-746 — the assigned-handoff
            # dev ran while its status-label echo queued a second dev).
            # The SM owns the loop from there; explicit dispatches
            # (inputs.leg) bypass this derive branch entirely.
            :
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" \
            || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' \
              || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"; slot="bug"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"; slot="story"
            fi

# Migrated from IstiN/dmtools-agents factory-sm.yml (f377609) — the
# agents-repo copy is DEPRECATED for new callers (kept only so existing
# pinned users like fa keep resolving their historical SHA).
#
# FREEZE CONTRACT: target repositories carry only a thin stub (schedule +
# this call) pinned to an immutable SHA of THIS repo. Agent code and the
# dmtools CLI are NOT tied to that SHA anymore — they resolve from RELEASES
# by version knobs (repo variables of the CALLER, per-repo, no workflow
# edits to bump):
#
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION   — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' or e.g.
#                           'agents-rel-20260928-…'); the agent pack
#                           (sm_github) is fetched from that release's
#                           asset catalog via the dmtools registry
#                           (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY). Default: latest.
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION  — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' or
#                           'vX.Y.Z'); installed from the release bundle.
#                           Default: latest.
#
# Runs in the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo,
# vars.* and secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own
# versions).
#
# What it does: resolves the two version knobs, installs the dmtools CLI
# (release asset, no repo file needed), then runs the SM rule engine as a
# VERSIONED AGENT PACK (dmtools run sm_github@latest) against the target
# repo's loop state — the pack carries smAgent.js + rules + engine closure,
# verified against the release's sha256 inventory.
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     schedule: [{cron: '*/10 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {dryRun: {type: boolean, default: true}}}
#   jobs:
#     sm:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}   # STRING —
#         # typed (boolean) reusable inputs reject expressions; strings take them.
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine SM'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      dryRun:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions, live bisect probes D/E)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login for #687 PR rules: excluded from review-external-once, gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews and the SM prMachineAuthor rules (auto legs, e.g. auto rework). Global-level knob — the agents repo carries no hardcoded login."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      silent-token:
        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows. Routed as an INPUT: GitHub delivers an EMPTY value when github.token is mapped through the reusable-call secrets block (live-verified), while inputs carry it; GitHub auto-masks token values in logs either way."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      ci-workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'quality.yml'
      validation-checks:
        description: "Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps these check names itself. JSON array as a STRING (e.g. '[\"agents-suite\",\"static\",\"gate\"]')."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      parallel-workers:
        description: "OPT-IN (dmtools Dart runtime only): runAsync worker-pool size for parallel READ fan-out inside the SM tick (per-PR/issue enrichment, dispatched-CI probes). '0'/absent = runAsync not wired — the engine takes its sequential fallback (Java/GraalJS parity), zero deviation. A value parsing to int >= 2 rides jobParams.parallelWorkers."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '0'
      state-publish:
        description: "OPT-IN factory-state publishing (owner 2026-09-23): JSON object {channel:'release', repo?, tag?, asset?}. The tick uploads factory-state.json as a public prerelease asset; the board (site/factory) reads the releases/latest CDN link. Empty = off."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the callee
# does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing declared one fails
# the guard test (factory_stub_ref_test.dart parity in each caller).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: "PAT for GitHub tool calls + gh CLI (SM engine + validation probes)."
        required: true
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN:
        description: "Optional dedicated silent-update token; the silent-token input wins when both are set."
        required: false

permissions:

  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net

        run: |
          resolve_tag() {
            local repo="$1" knob="$2"

blocks.text:
# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
